#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The --resolv-conf kubelet flag is not being validated by the ValidateKubeletConfiguration when kubelet starting (e.g.: the given file may not exist), which can lead to Pod DNS Policies no applying properly for the Pods spawned on the node.

I went back to the original comments that lead to this and I want to ask a deeper question (truly asking, not telling).

If I understand correctly, the way this operates today is:
* Accept any value for this flag
* When we start a pod
  - Try to open the file
  - Try to parse the file
  - If no error, merge some pod specific stuff
  - Start the pod

This has the upside that the host DNS file might change and new pods will get those changes.  It has the downside that it makes the failure mode runtime-only.  This PR seeks to make it fail at startup, but it only goes half-way.  It doesn't try to parse the file, and we still re-read the file at each pod startup, so it can still fail.

I think we should probably go all one direction or the other.  Either:

1) Do it all at runtime and document it
* Accept any value for this flag
* When we start a pod
  - Try to open the file
  - Try to parse the file
  - If no error, merge some pod specific stuff
  - Start the pod
  
2) Do it all at startup
* Verify this flag
  - open it, read it, parse it, save the result
  - if error, abort
* When we start a pod
  - use the saved values
  - merge some pod specific stuff
  - Start the pod

The advantag of 2 is that we have one less runtime failure mode.  Disadvantage is that it needs a kubelet restart to pick up changes (same as the kubelet config file itself).

@SergeyKanzhelev @mrunalp - opinion?
This probably should not be done in the API validation, but after that phase, while kubelt is starting up (cmd/kubelet/app/server.go)

1. is not what we have already?

2. sounds a breaking change in behavior that may impact someone

1 is what we have, meaning this PR should be abandoned

2 is, I guess, a little bit incompatible but it's not clear to me it is worse...

issue_context.title: ValidateKubeletConfiguration does not validate the ResolverConfig option
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

The ``--resolv-conf`` kubelet flag is not being validated by the ``ValidateKubeletConfiguration`` [1] (e.g.: the given file may not exist), which can lead to Pod DNS Policies no applying properly for the Pods spawned on the node.

[1] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/758b4641522ec279af99d218dba3deeca867b194/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/validation/validation.go#L43

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should fail fast if the set ``--resolv-conf`` flag is invalid.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Start Kubelet with an invalid flag.

### Anything else we need to know?

Problem raised in the comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110566/files#r1136100726

### Kubernetes version

Kubernetes v1.27 and older.
